qa_pairs.question: How can users view the available command-line options for `cfx5solve` when running Ansys CFX on Alliance clusters?
qa_pairs.answer: To view the command-line options for `cfx5solve`, users should first load the appropriate Ansys module version (matching the one in their Slurm script) and then execute `cfx5solve -help` from the command line.

qa_pairs.question: What are the default precision and mesh size capabilities of `cfx5solve` in Ansys CFX, and how can they be extended for more demanding simulations?
qa_pairs.answer: `cfx5solve` defaults to single-precision calculations and supports meshes up to 80 million structured elements or 200 million unstructured elements. For double precision, the `-double` option can be added (which doubles memory usage). To handle larger meshes, up to 2 billion elements, the `-large` option should be specified.

qa_pairs.question: How does `cfx5solve` automatically manage parallel execution using MPI for single-node versus multi-node Ansys CFX simulations on Alliance clusters?
qa_pairs.answer: For single-node simulations, `cfx5solve` defaults to "Open MPI Local Parallel" on Narval and Fir clusters, and "Intel MPI Local Parallel" on other clusters. When running multi-node simulations, it switches to "Open MPI Distributed Parallel" for Narval and Fir, and "Intel MPI Distributed Parallel" for other clusters. These methods are specified using the `-start-method` option in the Slurm scripts, along with appropriate MPI configurations.
